help.about.recon: Writes the names of the game’s HUD pieces to the BepInEx log so a developer can fix Game UI entries after a game update. Safe to press any time.
help.gameui.always: This part of the game HUD can be moved but not hidden, so you never lose your skills or HP bar mid-fight.
help.hotkeys.passthrough: When on, a key you bound to Stellar no longer also triggers the game action on the same key.
help.layout.snap: While dragging, a window jumps flush to a screen edge or another window once it is closer than the threshold.
help.layout.sticky: Alt + click a Stellar window keeps the cursor free after you let go of Alt. Click the game world or press Esc to return to the camera.
help.layout.threshold: How close (in pixels) a window must get before it snaps. 0 = only exact edges.
help.perf.perPlugin: Rate: give one plugin its own refresh rate instead of the global one. Self-rate lets the plugin speed itself up when it needs to: Boost = a short burst (ends after 10 s at most), Self-managed = the plugin picks its own rate.
help.perf.rate: Lower = more game FPS. Higher = smoother Stellar windows. 30 Hz is the default and suits most players.
help.perf.uncap: Turns off V-Sync and the game’s FPS limit so it runs as fast as your graphics card allows. More FPS, but more heat, fan noise and possible screen tearing.
help.themes.buttons: How buttons in older Stellar windows are drawn. House-style windows use their own rounded buttons. Watch the Classic button in the preview.
help.themes.font: Makes text in Stellar windows bigger or smaller. Window frames stay the same size.
help.themes.language: Language for Stellar windows. "Follow game client" uses the language the game is set to.
help.themes.opacity: How see-through Stellar windows are. Buttons and panels fade with the frame; text and pictures stay solid.
help.themes.scrollbar: Thumb = only the moving handle. Track = handle on a thin rail. Watch the list in the preview.
help.themes.ui: Scales whole Stellar windows: text, buttons and frames together.

perf.perPlugin.desc: Override how often each plugin refreshes. Self-rate lets a plugin drive its own update rate: Boost speeds it up briefly (released after a 10 s safety cap); Self-managed lets the plugin fully control and hold its own rate with no cap. Default is Off (follows the global rate).
perf.perPlugin.title: Per-plugin rate
perf.range.default: Near-full game FPS while Stellar still feels smooth. The sweet spot.
perf.range.high: Smoother Stellar windows than the default, at some game FPS cost.
perf.range.low: Best game FPS. Stellar windows refresh only 10–15 times a second, so they visibly lag.
perf.range.max: Smoothest, most responsive Stellar windows. Costs the most game FPS.
perf.rate.desc: How often Stellar refreshes its windows, HUD and input each second.
perf.rateDesc.default: Near-vanilla game FPS while keeping the HUD and input smooth enough that most players won't notice. The sweet spot.
perf.rateDesc.high: Smoother Stellar UI than the default, at some game-FPS cost — higher is smoother but more costly.
perf.rateDesc.low: Best game FPS — Stellar barely touches your frame rate. The HUD, cooldowns and on-screen info refresh only ~10-15×/sec, so they visibly lag and typing/dragging in Stellar feels delayed.
perf.rateDesc.max: Smoothest, most responsive Stellar UI — updates every rendered frame. Costs the most game FPS.
perf.uncap.capped: The game keeps its own FPS limit.
perf.uncap.desc: Removes the game's frame-rate cap (disables V-Sync + the FPS limit) so it runs as fast as your GPU allows. Higher FPS, but more GPU heat/power/fan noise and possible screen tearing.
perf.uncap.label: Uncap the game's frame rate
perf.uncap.warn: Uncapped: expect more GPU heat and possible tearing.
perf.updateRate.desc: How often Stellar refreshes its HUD, input and overlays each second. Lower = more game FPS; higher = smoother Stellar UI.
